patches.new: However, a **Registered Replication Report** published in 2016 by Wagenmakers and colleagues — seventeen independent laboratories running the procedure on nearly 1,900 participants — failed to reproduce the effect, casting doubt on the original finding. (This is a different project from the separate *Many Labs* replication series, which the two are often confused with.)

visual.title: The study that separates feeling from showing
visual.alt: A two-panel comparison of Ekman and Friesen's finding that Japanese and American viewers made the same faces watching a distressing film alone but diverged when an authority figure was present, with the Japanese viewers masking distress with smiles; four cards for the display rule operations of intensifying, deintensifying, neutralising and masking; and a side-by-side summary of the universalist and constructionist positions with the evidence each rests on.
visual.caption: Alone, no difference. Watched, a large one. The emotion was never the variable — the audience was.
